response.sql: WITH tc AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories o LEFT JOIN telescopes t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM telescopes), sh AS (SELECT tc.observstation, tc.telescope_count, tc.telescope_count * 1.0 / tot.total AS share FROM tc CROSS JOIN tot), avg_sh AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM sh), above AS (SELECT sh.observstation, sh.telescope_count, sh.share, sh.share - avg_sh.avg_share AS diff_above_avg FROM sh CROSS JOIN avg_sh WHERE sh.share > avg_sh.avg_share), ranked AS (SELECT above.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY diff_above_avg DESC) AS rk FROM above) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, diff_above_avg FROM ranked WHERE rk <= 10 ORDER BY diff_above_avg DESC;

assumptions.assumption: The average share is taken over every row in the observatories table, so observatories with zero telescopes count as share 0 in the average. Total telescopes is the row count of the telescopes table.
Ties at the 10th position are handled with RANK() over the difference, so every observatory whose difference equals the 10th-ranked difference is returned.
Share is computed as telescope_count * 1.0 / total so the division is not integer division and no rounding is applied.

alternatives.interpretation: The average share is taken only over observatories that have at least one telescope, so zero-telescope observatories are excluded from the average (they still cannot appear in the result, since their share is 0 and below any positive average).
